features: "Retinal 2K" is a 1920 x 1920 square frame — head-to-toe, not widescreen
140° x 140° field of view with up to 6x Enhanced Zoom
Charges three ways: USB-C, existing 8-24VAC doorbell wires, or Ring solar
Installs in about ten minutes with no wiring at all
Ring AI Pro trial in the box; nothing is recorded once it lapses

specs.resolution: Ring "Retinal 2K" = 1920 x 1920 (3.7MP) per Ring's own spec sheet — a square frame, not the 2560-pixel-wide 2K of the display standard
specs.powerSource: Built-in rechargeable lithium-ion battery; optional trickle charge from doorbell wires, USB-C or Ring solar accessories
specs.transformerRequirement: None required. If you do trickle-charge from existing wiring, Ring specifies an 8-24VAC supply — the most forgiving lower limit in this group
specs.batteryLife: Not published by Ring for this model; the spec page lists only "built-in rechargeable Lithium Ion battery" with no runtime figure or event count
specs.wifiBands: 2.4GHz only — Wi-Fi 4 (802.11n) single band. No 5GHz. Ring recommends 10 Mbps upload
specs.localStorage: None. No card slot, no hub option — recordings exist only in Ring's cloud
specs.subscriptionFree: Live View, two-way talk and motion notifications. No video is saved and no person/package alerts fire
specs.paywalledFeatures: All video history, Person/Package/Vehicle alerts and Extended Live View need Ring Solo ($4.99/mo, $49.99/yr, one device) or Multi ($9.99/mo); Familiar Faces, Video Descriptions and Video Search need Ring Pro ($19.99/mo)
specs.smartHomeSupport: Alexa only. No Google Home, no Apple Home, no Matter
specs.chimeIncluded: No. Alerts go to your phone and Alexa devices; a Ring Chime or an existing wired chime setup costs extra

pros: The square 1:1 frame genuinely shows a visitor head-to-toe and a parcel on the mat, which the widescreen SimpliSafe and Wyze cannot
Three charging routes — USB-C, 8-24VAC doorbell wires, solar — and the 8V lower limit accepts older transformers that the Nest, Wyze and Lorex reject
Ring's motion processing and app remain the most polished here, and Alexa devices announce the doorbell without extra hardware
$99.99 buys the mainstream default a buyer is searching for, with the largest accessory and mount ecosystem
cons: Without a Ring plan it is an intercom: nothing is recorded, and person and package alerts are switched off entirely
"Retinal 2K" is 1920 x 1920 — the same pixel count as Blink's $39.99 doorbell, and fewer pixels than the 5MP Reolink or Tapo
2.4GHz Wi-Fi 4 only, while the $249.99 Pro in the same lineup gets dual-band Wi-Fi 6
Ring publishes no battery runtime figure at all, so there is no manufacturer number to hold them to
No local storage of any kind, so a lapsed subscription means the footage is simply gone
shortTagline: The default pick — but "2K" is 1920x1920 and nothing records without a plan.

material: Polycarbonate with a polished metal-effect faceplate
features: 2880 x 2880 sensor — the highest pixel count of any battery doorbell here
Wi-Fi 6 dual-band radio; the only Ring doorbell in the range with 5GHz
Quick Release Ultra Battery Pack swaps out without unmounting the doorbell
10x Enhanced Zoom into the 8.3MP frame
140° x 140° head-to-toe view with Ring's Search Party and AI features

specs.resolution: Ring "Retinal 4K" = 2880 x 2880 (8.3MP) per Ring's EU technical specifications. That is 2880 pixels across, not the 3840 of UHD — it is called 4K on total pixel count, not width
specs.powerSource: Quick Release Ultra Battery Pack (removable, rechargeable)
specs.transformerRequirement: None — battery only. The Ultra pack is a new format and is not interchangeable with older Ring battery packs
specs.batteryLife: Not published by Ring. Tom's Guide lost under 25% in two weeks of testing; SafeWise's tester on a high-traffic porch reported recharging "about every 2 weeks"
specs.wifiBands: Dual-band 2.4/5GHz, Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax). Ring recommends a minimum 15 Mbps upload — the highest requirement in this group
specs.subscriptionFree: Live View and two-way talk. Nothing is recorded, and no smart alerts fire
specs.paywalledFeatures: Video history to 180 days and Person/Package/Vehicle alerts need Ring Solo ($4.99/mo) or Multi ($9.99/mo); Familiar Faces, Video Descriptions, Video Search and 24/7 professional monitoring need Ring Pro ($19.99/mo, $199.99/yr)
specs.smartHomeSupport: Alexa and Alexa+. No Google Home, no Apple Home, no Matter
specs.chimeIncluded: No — a Ring Chime or an Alexa device is needed for an in-home ring

pros: 8.3MP of real sensor, so the 10x zoom actually resolves a face or a plate rather than smearing
The only battery doorbell here with Wi-Fi 6 and a 5GHz radio, which matters on congested 2.4GHz streets
Quick Release battery pack means a swap in seconds instead of taking the doorbell off the wall to charge
Tom's Guide measured under 25% drain in a fortnight on a normal porch — genuinely long-lived when traffic is light
cons: $249.99 buys a camera that records nothing at all until you also pay Ring monthly — the single worst price-to-freedom ratio in this comparison
"4K" is 2880 x 2880, narrower than UHD's 3840 across; it is a square frame counted on total pixels
SafeWise's high-traffic test porch needed a recharge roughly every two weeks, which is nothing like the "months" buyers assume
Needs 15 Mbps upload to behave; Tom's Guide saw it stumble below that
The new Ultra battery pack does not fit any older Ring camera, so existing spares are useless
shortTagline: Genuinely 8.3MP and Wi-Fi 6, but $250 of camera that saves nothing without a plan.

features: Free tier includes person, package, vehicle and animal alerts — no subscription
6 hours of event video previews stored free
2K HDR with a 166° diagonal view and digital zoom-and-crop
Gemini for Home video descriptions and natural-language search on the Advanced plan
Dual-band 802.11ac Wi-Fi, unusual at this price

specs.resolution: Google's store page states only "2K HDR" with no pixel count; Tom's Guide's review gives 2048 x 2048 at 30fps
specs.aspectRatio: Sources conflict: Google's tech-spec page lists 1:1, while Tom's Guide's review says 3:4 — though the 2048 x 2048 figure in that same review is 1:1
specs.fieldOfView: 166° diagonal, with visible barrel distortion at the edges per Tom's Guide
specs.powerSource: Hardwired only — no battery in this generation, so a power cut takes the doorbell offline
specs.transformerRequirement: 16-24VAC, 10-40VA, 50/60Hz doorbell transformer required. Google says the transformer and chime are sold separately and existing hardware may need replacing; an indoor plug-in adapter is a separate purchase
specs.localStorage: None. No card slot, no local NVR path
specs.subscriptionFree: 6 hours of event video previews (clips up to 10 seconds) plus free on-device person, package, vehicle and animal alerts and activity zones — the most generous free tier in this comparison
specs.paywalledFeatures: 30 days of event history and Familiar Faces need Google Home Premium Standard ($10/mo, $100/yr); 60 days of history, 10 days of 24/7 continuous recording and the Gemini descriptions and video search need Advanced ($20/mo, $200/yr)
specs.smartHomeSupport: Google Home and Gemini for Home. No Alexa, no Apple Home, no Matter — and Matter would not carry the video stream anyway
specs.chimeIncluded: No. Drives your existing wired chime, and Google Home speakers and displays can announce visitors

pros: The only cloud doorbell here whose person, package, vehicle and animal alerts cost nothing — Ring, Arlo and Wyze all charge for the equivalent
Six hours of free event history means a missed delivery is still there when you get home
Dual-band 802.11ac where the $99.99 Ring is stuck on single-band Wi-Fi 4
Gemini descriptions and plain-English video search are the most useful AI layer of any doorbell in this set
cons: The 16-24VAC, 10-40VA transformer requirement is the strictest here — plenty of older US homes run 8-10VAC and need an electrician or Google's separate plug-in adapter
Wired only, with no battery backup, so it dies with the power
Google publishes no pixel count for its "2K", and its own aspect-ratio spec (1:1) contradicts Tom's Guide's review (3:4)
Zero local storage and no NVR path, so everything depends on Google keeping the service running
Google Home ecosystem only — no Alexa, no Apple Home
shortTagline: Free person and package alerts beat Ring outright — if your transformer hits 16VAC.

features: Two cameras: a forward lens plus a dedicated downward lens for the doormat
8GB of storage inside the doorbell — no hub, no card, no fee
Delivery Guard package detection and face recognition run on-device
Runs on a removable USB-C battery or on existing doorbell wiring
Dual-light colour night vision to about 16 ft

specs.resolution: Sources conflict: eufy's own E340 specification article gives main camera 2048 x 1536 and second camera 1600 x 1200 (which eufy labels "1080p" although it is 4:3); B&H's listing for the same SKU claims 2560 x 1920 / 4MP. eufy markets both lenses simply as "2K"
specs.aspectRatio: 4:3 on both cameras. There is no single head-to-toe frame — the second, downward-facing camera is what covers the doorstep
specs.fieldOfView: Not published by eufy in its E340 specification article, and absent from B&H's and eufy's own listings
specs.powerSource: Removable USB-C rechargeable battery, or hardwired. eufy requires the battery to stay installed even in wired mode
specs.transformerRequirement: Sources conflict: eufy's product page says "8 to 24V and >10VA", while eufy's own E340 specification support article says "Existing Doorbell Wiring (16-24V, 10VA) or 19V-0.6A DC Power Adapter"
specs.batteryLife: eufy publishes no month figure for the E340. Linkd Home's 30-day heavy-use test ended at 74% and projected roughly 78 days to shutdown
specs.wifiBands: 2.4GHz only (802.11 b/g/n), plus a 433MHz radio for eufy chimes
specs.localStorage: 8GB eMMC inside the doorbell with no card slot — around 90 days at 30 twenty-second clips a day. Expanding it means buying a HomeBase S280 or S380 separately
specs.subscriptionFree: Everything. Recording, playback, human detection, Delivery Guard package detection and face recognition all run locally with no plan
specs.paywalledFeatures: Nothing essential — eufy sells optional cloud backup only
specs.smartHomeSupport: Alexa and Google Assistant. No Apple HomeKit, no Matter
specs.chimeIncluded: Not on this SKU. It drives an existing mechanical chime, a eufy HomeBase, or a smart speaker; the chime bundle is a separate purchase

pros: The second, downward camera is the only genuinely different answer to the parcel problem here — everyone else stretches one lens into a tall frame
8GB on the doorbell itself means no hub, no card and no monthly fee, unlike Blink and Arlo whose local storage needs a base station
Works battery or wired, and the battery pops out on USB-C instead of coming off the wall
Face recognition and package detection run on the device — the same features Ring charges $19.99/mo for
cons: eufy's own two sources disagree on the wiring requirement (8-24V vs 16-24V) and on the sensor resolution, which is careless for a $150 device
2.4GHz Wi-Fi only, and Linkd Home measured 13.6 seconds average notification latency with thumbnails
No field-of-view figure is published anywhere, so you cannot compare its coverage on paper
No Apple HomeKit and no Matter, so Apple households are locked out
eufy's history of cloud-privacy incidents is a real consideration for a camera pointed at your front door
shortTagline: Two cameras and 8GB on board — the cleanest no-subscription answer to package theft.

model: Aqara Video Doorbell G410 (Doorbell Camera Hub G410)
features: Native HomeKit Secure Video — the only doorbell here with it
mmWave radar for presence and lingering detection, not just PIR
On-device face recognition with no subscription and no cloud upload
Doubles as a Zigbee 3.0 hub, a Thread border router and a Matter controller
USB-C chime repeater and six AA cells are in the box

specs.resolution: 2K, 2304 x 1296 (about 3MP) from an f/1.8 lens. Streamed through Apple Home it is downgraded: Aqara states "When using the HSV, the maximum resolution is 1200p"
specs.aspectRatio: Sources conflict: Aqara's product page lists a 4:3 aspect ratio, but the 2304 x 1296 output it quotes on the same page is 16:9
specs.powerSource: Six AA alkaline cells (supplied) or hardwired 12-24V AC 0.2A / 12-24V DC 0.5A
specs.transformerRequirement: Optional. If you hardwire it, Aqara specifies 12-24VAC — it will not run from an 8VAC transformer, but it is happier than the 16VAC-minimum Nest, Wyze and Lorex
specs.batteryLife: Aqara claims up to 5 months on the six supplied AA cells. Aqara does not publish the daily event count that figure assumes
specs.localStorage: microSD up to 512GB in the doorbell itself, plus NAS backup. No separate hub or base station needed
specs.subscriptionFree: Everything that matters: microSD recording, on-device face recognition, mmWave presence detection and HomeKit Secure Video (which uses your iCloud+ storage, not Aqara's)
specs.paywalledFeatures: Only Aqara's optional HomeGuardian cloud plan; HKSV needs an iCloud+ plan and an Apple home hub, which most Apple households already have
specs.smartHomeSupport: HomeKit Secure Video (requires an Apple home hub), Alexa, Google Home, SmartThings and Home Assistant. It is a Matter controller and Thread border router for other devices — but Matter carries no video, so the camera reaches Apple Home through HKSV, not through Matter
specs.chimeIncluded: Yes — a USB-C powered 95dB chime repeater ships in the box

pros: The only genuine HomeKit Secure Video doorbell here, and it stores to iCloud+ rather than to another vendor's paid cloud
mmWave radar catches someone loitering that a PIR sensor sleeps through — no other doorbell in this set has it
Buys you a Zigbee hub, a Thread border router and a Matter controller in the same $145 as the doorbell
Cheap replaceable AA cells rather than a proprietary pack, and a real microSD slot up to 512GB
Chime is included, which Ring, Arlo, Blink and eufy all make you buy separately
cons: HomeKit Secure Video caps the stream at 1200p, so Apple users never see the 2K the box advertises
Aqara's own page gives a 4:3 aspect ratio next to a 16:9 sensor output — one of them is wrong
The "Matter" badge is about the hub, not the camera: no Matter controller will ever show you this doorbell's video
The five-month AA claim comes with no stated event count, so it is untestable as a promise
175° of wide angle at 3MP means noticeably less detail per degree than the 5MP Reolink or Tapo
shortTagline: Real HomeKit Secure Video plus a Zigbee/Thread hub — but Apple Home caps it at 1200p.

features: 1944 x 1944 square sensor with HDR and a 180° diagonal view
Built-in 80dB siren — rare on a doorbell at any price
Runs on its internal battery or on existing doorbell wiring
Apple Home support arrived for 2nd-gen Arlo devices in March 2025
Direct-to-Wi-Fi: no Arlo SmartHub needed for basic operation

specs.resolution: 2K, 1944 x 1944 (3.8MP) with HDR, per Tom's Guide's spec table
specs.fieldOfView: 180° diagonal — the widest in this comparison
specs.powerSource: Built-in non-removable rechargeable lithium-ion battery, or hardwired to existing doorbell wiring
specs.transformerRequirement: Optional. Arlo does not publish a voltage range on its US product page; the doorbell is designed to install on standard existing chime wiring
specs.batteryLife: Arlo claims up to 6 months, explicitly "dependent on usage", and publishes no event count. Tom's Guide frames that as light use only
specs.wifiBands: 2.4GHz only, per Tom's Guide's specification table
specs.localStorage: None in the doorbell. Local backup exists only if you also buy an Arlo SmartHub or Base Station, sold separately
specs.subscriptionFree: Live view and basic motion notification. Tom's Guide: without a plan it is "stripped to a grossly basic live view and motion detector functionality"
specs.paywalledFeatures: 30-day cloud history, custom activity zones, person/package/vehicle/animal recognition, lock-screen clip previews and emergency response all require Arlo Secure — raised twice, to $7.99/mo for one camera and $12.99/mo for unlimited
specs.smartHomeSupport: Alexa, Google Home and Apple Home. Arlo's community manager confirmed Apple Home integration for 2nd-generation devices in March 2025 after a long delay. No Matter video
specs.chimeIncluded: No on the 1-cam SKU. It can drive an existing wired chime, or Arlo sells Chime 2 separately

pros: 180° diagonal is the widest view here, and it is a square 1:1 frame rather than a letterbox
The only doorbell in this set with a built-in 80dB siren you can trigger from the app
Works with Alexa, Google Home and Apple Home — the broadest ecosystem coverage of any non-Aqara model here
$79.99 for a battery-or-wired 2K doorbell undercuts Ring's equivalent by $20
cons: The harshest subscription cliff in this comparison — no plan means no zones, no person alerts and no saved clips at all
Arlo Secure has been raised twice, from $2.99 to $4.99 to $7.99 a month for a single camera
The battery is not removable: recharging means taking the whole doorbell off the wall
Local storage requires an Arlo SmartHub or Base Station that is not in the box
2.4GHz only, and Arlo publishes no wired voltage range on its US page
shortTagline: Widest view and a siren for $80 — then Arlo Secure takes almost everything else.

features: 24/7 continuous recording to microSD at no monthly cost
Chime controller unit included — drives your existing mechanical chime
Starlight sensor for colour night vision
2048 x 1536 sensor, marketed as 2K
18-month warranty if bought direct from wyze.com instead of 12

specs.resolution: "2K" = 2048 x 1536 (3.1MP) at 20fps by day and 15fps at night — a 4:3 frame, well short of a 2560-wide 2K
specs.aspectRatio: 4:3 — landscape, not head-to-toe. A parcel placed against the door can sit below the frame
specs.fieldOfView: 135° horizontal, 103° vertical, 166.8° diagonal — the narrowest horizontal view here
specs.powerSource: Hardwired only. There is no battery option and no battery backup
specs.transformerRequirement: 16-24V AC, 10VA or more. An 8-10VAC transformer, common in older US homes, will not run it — Ring's 8-24VAC and SimpliSafe's 8-24VAC will
specs.localStorage: microSD up to 256GB, including 24/7 continuous recording, at no charge. The card is not in the box unless you buy the bundle
specs.subscriptionFree: Live view, two-way talk, real-time motion alerts, 12-second event clips on a doorbell press, 3-6 seconds of pre-roll, and full 24/7 recording to your own microSD
specs.paywalledFeatures: Person and package detection, full-length event clips and motion-activated voice prompts require Cam Plus ($2.99/mo per camera) or Cam Unlimited ($9.99/mo, $99/yr)
specs.smartHomeSupport: Alexa and Google Assistant. No Apple Home, no Matter
specs.chimeIncluded: Yes — a chime controller unit ships in the box and lets the doorbell ring your existing mechanical chime

pros: 24/7 continuous local recording for $59.98 and no monthly fee — nothing else here does that under $100
The chime controller is in the box, so your existing indoor chime keeps working; Blink's cheaper doorbell disables yours
Colour night vision from a starlight sensor rather than flat infrared
Wyze extends the warranty to 18 months when you buy from wyze.com rather than a retailer
cons: 16-24VAC minimum shuts out older 8-10VAC transformers — the same barrier as the Nest, on a $60 doorbell
135° horizontal and a 4:3 frame: the least head-to-toe coverage in this comparison, and no package framing to speak of
20fps by day, 15fps at night, so fast movement smears
Person and package detection are Cam Plus features — the free tier only gives you a 12-second clip when someone presses the button
Wired only, with no battery fallback, and Wyze's record on app outages and security incidents is uneven
shortTagline: $60 for 24/7 local recording — if your transformer makes 16VAC and you can live with 4:3.

features: 5MP 2560 x 1920 sensor — a real 2K-class pixel count, not a relabelled 1920 square
Open RTSP and ONVIF, so Home Assistant, Blue Iris and a NAS can record it
Indoor plug-in adapter in the box for homes with no doorbell wiring
Reolink Chime included
2-year warranty, double everyone else here except SimpliSafe with a plan

specs.resolution: 5MP, 2560 x 1920 at 20fps (H.264) — genuinely more pixels across than any of the "2K" square-frame doorbells here (Ring, Arlo and Blink are all under 2000 px wide)
specs.aspectRatio: Depends which one you buy: Reolink states the black unit shoots 4:3 landscape and the white unit shoots 3:4 vertical head-to-toe. Same model name, different framing
specs.powerSource: Hardwired. 12-24VAC 50/60Hz or 24V DC; an indoor power adapter is supplied for homes with no doorbell wiring at all
specs.transformerRequirement: 12-24VAC, or none — the supplied plug-in adapter means this is one of the few wired doorbells here that does not need an existing transformer
specs.localStorage: microSD up to 256GB in the doorbell, plus Reolink NVR/Home Hub, FTP and NAS. ONVIF and RTSP are open, so third-party recorders work
specs.subscriptionFree: Everything: person, vehicle and animal detection, 24/7 recording and full playback are free. Reolink states no monthly fees are required
specs.paywalledFeatures: Nothing. Reolink's cloud plan is entirely optional
specs.smartHomeSupport: Alexa, Google Assistant, Home Assistant, ONVIF and RTSP. No Apple Home, no Matter
specs.chimeIncluded: Yes — the Reolink Chime is in the box, and Echo Show and Google displays also work

pros: 5MP with dual-band Wi-Fi, no subscription and a chime in the box — the best raw hardware-per-dollar here
RTSP and ONVIF are open, so Home Assistant, Blue Iris, Frigate or a NAS can record it and you never depend on Reolink's cloud
The 12-24VAC range plus a supplied indoor adapter means it installs where the 16VAC-minimum Nest, Wyze and Lorex cannot
Two-year warranty, twice the category norm
cons: The white and black units frame differently (3:4 vs 4:3) under one product name — buy the wrong colour and you lose head-to-toe coverage
Wired only, with no battery version at this SKU
No Apple Home and no Matter; the app and integrations are aimed at the Home Assistant crowd, not the Apple one
H.264 at 20fps only, so motion is less fluid than the 25-30fps Ring and Nest models
Street pricing swings widely — Reolink's own US store lists $139.99 while Newegg has listed it at $129.99
shortTagline: 5MP, dual-band, RTSP open and zero fees — the self-hoster's doorbell.

features: $39.99 for a 1:1 head-to-toe frame — the cheapest doorbell in this comparison
1920 x 1920 at up to 25fps with improved dynamic range
Works on your Wi-Fi with no Sync Module required
Local save to a Sync Module 2 USB drive or Sync Module XR microSD, no plan needed
AI Smart Video Descriptions on Blink's Basic AI plan

specs.resolution: Blink markets "2K+"; its own technical specifications page says "1920p" — a 1920 x 1920 square frame, the same pixel count as Ring's $99.99 "Retinal 2K", at up to 25fps
specs.powerSource: Wired only — Blink states "Wired only (no batteries)"
specs.transformerRequirement: 12-24V AC in the US (8-24V AC in EU/UK), or Blink's optional plug-in adapter. Critically, Blink's FAQ says the doorbell "does not ring your existing in-home mechanical chime" and that a bypass cable must be fitted at the chime, which disables it
specs.wifiBands: 2.4GHz only (802.11 b/g/n); Blink asks for 2-6 Mbps upload depending on quality
specs.localStorage: Only via a Sync Module 2 (USB drive) or Sync Module XR (microSD), both sold separately. Nothing is stored in the doorbell itself
specs.subscriptionFree: Live view, motion alerts and two-way audio, plus local saving if you own a Sync Module
specs.paywalledFeatures: Cloud clips, Person Detection, Vehicle Detection and the AI Smart Video Descriptions all need a Blink plan: Basic $3.99/mo, Basic AI $6.99/mo, Plus $11.99/mo, Plus AI $19.99/mo
specs.smartHomeSupport: Alexa only. No Google Home, no Apple Home, no Matter
specs.chimeIncluded: No — and it will not drive your existing mechanical chime. Blink's FAQ requires "a Blink Mini, Blink Chime, or compatible Alexa device (each sold separately)" for an in-home alert

pros: $39.99 buys the same 1920 x 1920 square sensor Ring charges $99.99 for in the Battery Doorbell 2K
No Sync Module required to work — it joins your Wi-Fi directly, unlike older Blink doorbells
Local saving to a Sync Module needs no subscription, which Arlo cannot match at any price
25fps is the highest frame rate among the budget models here
cons: It cannot ring your existing mechanical chime — Blink's own FAQ says a bypass cable must be installed, which disables the chime permanently. You then have to buy a Blink Chime or an Echo
Local storage means buying a Sync Module 2 or XR separately, so the real entry price is well above $39.99
Person and Vehicle Detection are subscription features; with no plan it only tells you "motion"
Alexa-only, wired-only, 2.4GHz-only — the narrowest capability set in this comparison
"2K+" describes a 1920-pixel-wide frame, which is 1080p's width made square
shortTagline: $40 and a real 1:1 frame — but it kills your indoor chime and needs a Sync Module to record.

features: Integrates directly with a SimpliSafe alarm and its professional monitoring
162° wide-angle HDR view
8-24VAC transformer range — accepts older, weaker doorbell power
Free plan gives live view and a 7-day activity timeline
Warranty extends to 3 years while a qualifying SimpliSafe plan is active

specs.resolution: 1080p — the only sub-2K doorbell in this comparison, at a $169 price
specs.aspectRatio: 16:9 widescreen. There is no head-to-toe framing, so a parcel set against the door can fall below the frame
specs.powerSource: Hardwired only — no battery, no battery backup
specs.transformerRequirement: 8-24 VAC, 30VA maximum. SimpliSafe supports mechanical chimes only and states that digital chimes are not supported
specs.localStorage: None. No card slot and no local recorder option
specs.subscriptionFree: Live view in the app, real-time motion alerts and a 7-day activity timeline. Nothing is recorded
specs.paywalledFeatures: Every saved recording. The cheapest qualifying plan is Self Monitoring with Camera Recordings at $9.99/mo for up to 10 cameras with 30 days of rolling footage; professional monitoring costs more
specs.smartHomeSupport: Alexa and Google Assistant, plus deep integration with the SimpliSafe alarm system. No Apple Home, no Matter
specs.chimeIncluded: No — it uses your existing mechanical chime, and digital chimes are explicitly unsupported

pros: The only doorbell here that arms, disarms and triggers alongside a full professionally-monitored alarm system
8-24VAC is one of the most forgiving power ranges in the group, so it installs where the Nest and Wyze will not
Runs standalone without a SimpliSafe base station if you only want the doorbell
A qualifying subscription extends the hardware warranty from 1 year to as much as 3
cons: 1080p and 16:9 in 2026, for $169 — a $39.99 Blink has more pixels and a better-shaped frame
The cheapest plan that records anything is $9.99/mo, more than double Ring's $4.99 entry tier
Digital chimes are unsupported, which quietly disqualifies a lot of newer homes
SafeWise's testing found audio lag that makes real conversation hard and night vision that fades past roughly six feet
No local storage, no Apple Home, no Matter, and a design that has not changed since 2019
shortTagline: Buy it for the alarm integration, not the camera — it is still 1080p widescreen at $169.

model: TP-Link Tapo D230S1 Battery Video Doorbell Kit
features: 5MP 2560 x 1920 sensor — 2K done with real pixels
6700mAh removable battery rated up to 180 days at 10-20 events a day
H200 hub in the box doubles as the chime and holds the microSD card
Free on-device person, pet, vehicle and package detection
Colour night vision to roughly 25 ft

specs.resolution: 2K 5MP, 2560 x 1920, from a 1/2.7in sensor with an f/2.1 lens, at 15fps
specs.aspectRatio: 4:3 — TP-Link markets it as head-to-toe, but it is a landscape-leaning frame, not the 1:1 of the Ring, Arlo and Blink
specs.powerSource: Removable 6700mAh Tapo A100 lithium-ion battery, charged over USB-C
specs.transformerRequirement: None, and none supported on this kit: the doorbell is battery-only and the supplied H200 hub plugs into a mains socket (9V/0.85A adapter). There is no hardwired doorbell option
specs.batteryLife: Up to 180 days — and TP-Link publishes the assumption, which almost nobody else does: 10-20 events per day
specs.wifiBands: 2.4GHz only (802.11 b/g/n). The doorbell talks to the H200 hub; the hub joins your network
specs.localStorage: microSD up to 512GB in the included H200 hub. The card itself is not supplied
specs.subscriptionFree: Local recording to the hub's microSD, plus free on-device person, pet, vehicle and package detection
specs.paywalledFeatures: Cloud video storage, rich notifications with snapshots and extended history need a Tapo Care plan
specs.smartHomeSupport: Alexa and Google Home. No Apple Home, no Matter
specs.chimeIncluded: Yes — the H200 hub is the chime and it is in the box

pros: The only manufacturer here that states the event count behind its battery claim — 180 days at 10-20 events a day, which is a number you can actually test
5MP is a real 2K sensor, not a 1920-square frame relabelled
Hub, chime and microSD slot are all in the box; Blink, Arlo and Ring all charge extra for the equivalent
Person, pet, vehicle and package detection run on the device with no Tapo Care plan

specs.resolution: 8MP, 2160 x 3840 — a true 4K-class pixel count, but rotated: 2160 across and 3840 tall
specs.aspectRatio: 9:16 vertical portrait — the tallest frame in this comparison. Best in the group for seeing a parcel on the mat, worst for seeing across a wide porch
specs.fieldOfView: 150° diagonal — the narrowest here, against 180° on the Arlo and Reolink
specs.powerSource: Hardwired only — no battery and no battery backup
specs.transformerRequirement: 16-24VAC required, so an older 8-10VAC transformer will not run it
specs.localStorage: 32GB microSD card pre-installed in the doorbell, upgradable to 256GB. No cloud subscription of any kind is offered or needed
specs.subscriptionFree: Everything: recording, playback and person, vehicle, animal and package detection are all local and free
specs.paywalledFeatures: Nothing — Lorex charges no monthly fee for this model
specs.smartHomeSupport: Alexa and Google Assistant, through the older Lorex Classic app. No Apple Home, no Matter
specs.chimeIncluded: Yes — a chime kit ships in the box along with mounting wedges and connecting wires

pros: 8MP is the highest pixel count in this comparison and it costs $63 less than Ring's 4K Pro — with no subscription at all
A 32GB card is already fitted, so it records out of the box with nothing else to buy
Package, person, vehicle and animal detection are free, where Ring and Arlo both charge monthly for the same list
Chime kit, wedges and wiring included, and dual-band Wi-Fi at a price where most rivals are 2.4GHz only
cons: 150° diagonal is the narrowest view here — the tall 9:16 frame trades width for height
16-24VAC hardwired only, with no battery option and no battery backup
The Lorex Classic app is dated next to Ring's or Google's, and there is no Apple Home or Matter support
Lorex's own product page has listed the doorbell as available only through direct contact with its sales team, so retail stock can be patchy
32GB fills quickly at 4K, so most buyers will want to swap the card immediately
shortTagline: 8MP and a card in the box for $187, with no subscription — but only 150° wide.
